full_judgment: 5. Mr. Md. Ismail, the learned Advocate has appeared for the appellants and Mr. AKM Shamsul Karim, AAG along with Mr. Md. Hefzul Bari have appeared for the State. The learned Advocate for the appellants after taking us through the First Information Report, the charge, the evidences, the impugned judgment and also other materials on record, firstly, submits that it is in fact a case of no evidence against the appellants and they have been most illegally and improperly convicted and sentenced. He does not dispute the commission of the dacoity as alleged. His main contention is that the appellants are in no way connected with the commission of the alleged dacoity. The Sessions Judge has based conviction of the appellants solely on the so-called confession of co-accused Shahid Hossain alias Shafi and apart from the said confession there is no other evidence on record to connect the appellants in the commission of the dacoity. His further submission is that said confession which has been marked as exhibit No. 6 is absolutely vague, indefinite and partly exculpatory and partly inculpatory. The learned Additional Sessions Judge without coming to any finding as to whether the said confession is true and voluntary,  illegally passed the conviction of the appellants on the basis of such confessional statement. According to the learned Advocate for the appellants, the said confession is neither true nor voluntary and the same was extracted from its maker appellant Shahid Hossain through torture and duress. The next submission of the learned Advocate for the appellants is that even if for argument's sake, the confession is found to be we and voluntary, still it may at best be a basis for conviction of its maker and other co-accused appellants without any other independent trustworthy, corroborative evidence on record. Hence on the face of it, it is clear that in the absence of any other reliable corroborative evidence, the appellants Kabir, Sattar and Abdul Matin ought not to have been convicted merely on the basis of the so-called confession of appellant Shahid Hossain and hence the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence as against the aforesaid 3 co-accused appellants cannot be sustained in law. Further, submission of the learned Advocate for the appellants is that in examining appellant Shahid Hossain under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, this so-called confession was not brought to his notice and he has been deprived of giving any explanation to the alleged confession or denying the same and naturally the appellant Shahid Hossain as well as other appellants have been seriously prejudiced thereby and as such the so-called confession should not be the basis of conviction of the appellants. In this connection the learned Advocate for the appellants further submits that one Badrul Islam, the police officer who had done the main part of the investigation in this case, and produced the accused appellant Shahid Hossain before the Magistrate for recording the alleged confession, examined the witnesses under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, seized alamats of the occurrence, has been withheld and not produced by the prosecution without any explanation though he was a charge-sheet material witness in this case. Hence it is contended that the trial Court ought to have drawn an adverse presumption against the genuineness of the prosecution case.
